"You are an expert AAA game-development team. Create a high-quality, fully playable 3D first-person fighting game with intense hand-to-hand combat, satisfying hit reactions, blood effects, advanced animations, and intelligent enemies.
The game should feel like a combination of a first-person martial arts brawler and a brutal action fighting game. Prioritize responsive combat, fluid animations, immersive sound, and high-quality visuals.
1. CORE GAMEPLAY
First-person perspective with visible player arms and hands.
Real-time hand-to-hand combat.
Light attacks, heavy attacks, uppercuts, kicks, blocks, parries, and dodges.
Multiple attack combinations that chain together.
Different fighting styles that players can unlock.
Enemies react differently depending on where and how they are hit.
A satisfying combo system with score multipliers.
Powerful finishing moves when enemies are weakened.
Enemies can attack, block, dodge, flank, and counterattack.
2. COMBAT SYSTEM
Build a deep combat system with:
Left and right punches.
Hooks, jabs, crosses, elbows, and uppercuts.
Front kicks, roundhouse kicks, and heavy kicks.
Blocking and perfectly timed parries.
Quick dodges and counterattacks.
Stamina and attack cooldowns.
Hit detection based on distance, direction, and timing.
Combo chains with different animations.
Enemy stagger, knockback, stumbling, and knockdown reactions.
Camera shake and impact effects for heavy hits.
Every attack must have its own animation, timing, damage, sound, and impact effect.
3. BLOOD AND DAMAGE EFFECTS
Include stylized, convincing blood effects:
Blood particles when attacks connect.
Small blood splashes and temporary blood decals.
Blood effects on walls and floors.
Visible bruising and damage effects where practical.
Stronger effects for powerful attacks.
Blood effects that fade over time.
Enemy hit reactions that match the attack location.
Keep the effects visually impactful without relying on excessive graphic gore.
4. ENEMY AI
Create several types of intelligent enemies:
Basic fighters.
Fast and aggressive enemies.
Heavy enemies with powerful attacks.
Defensive enemies that block and counter.
Boss enemies with unique movesets.
Enemies should:
Approach and attack the player intelligently.
Avoid endlessly repeating the same attack.
React to player combos.
Block or dodge occasionally.
Coordinate attacks when multiple enemies are present.
Have health, stamina, and individual fighting styles.
5. VISUAL QUALITY
Aim for polished, high-quality 3D graphics:
Detailed environments and realistic lighting.
High-quality character models.
Smooth first-person hand animations.
Detailed enemy animations.
Shadows, reflections, and atmospheric effects.
Impact particles and motion trails.
Immersive camera movement.
High-quality materials and textures.
Use a consistent visual style. Do not use placeholder cubes or unfinished-looking characters for the main gameplay.
6. GAME MODES
Include:
Story Mode: Fight through multiple arenas and increasingly difficult enemies.
Survival Mode: Fight endless waves of enemies.
Training Mode: Practice attacks, combos, dodges, and parries.
Boss Mode: Fight challenging enemies with special movesets.
7. PROGRESSION
Add:
Player XP and leveling.
Unlockable fighting styles.
New attacks and combos.
Upgradable health and stamina.
Currency earned from fights.
A shop for unlocking combat abilities and cosmetic items.
Difficulty progression.
8. MOBILE CONTROLS
The game must be designed for Android phones and mobile browsers.
Include:
Left virtual joystick for movement.
Right-side swipe area for camera movement.
Separate punch, kick, block, dodge, and heavy attack buttons.
A special attack button.
Responsive touch input.
Adjustable sensitivity.
A customizable control layout.
UI that adapts to different screen sizes.
Controls must be comfortable and responsive on a touchscreen.
9. SOUND DESIGN
Add:
Punch and kick impact sounds.
Enemy pain and reaction sounds.
Footsteps.
Blocking and parrying sounds.
Heavy attack sound effects.
Arena ambience.
Music that changes intensity during combat.
Attacks should sound powerful and distinct.
10. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
If creating a browser game:
Deliver a playable, self-contained HTML file whenever possible.
Use Three.js r128 through a CDN for 3D rendering.
Avoid ES module imports.
Use optimized models, textures, effects, and animations.
Optimize performance for Android phones.
Include a quality setting: Low, Medium, High, and Ultra.
Use touch controls by default on mobile.
Include a working main menu, pause menu, settings, and restart system.
11. QUALITY REQUIREMENTS
Do not create a basic prototype and call it finished.
The following must actually work:
Combat and hit detection.
Player movement and camera control.
Enemy AI and attacks.
Health and stamina.
Blocking, dodging, and parrying.
Combos and finishers.
Blood and impact effects.
Game modes and progression.
Mobile touch controls.
Do not include fake buttons, nonfunctional systems, or unfinished menu options.
Build the game in organized, maintainable systems. Test the complete gameplay loop, fix bugs, and prioritize a polished experience.
FINAL GOAL: Create an immersive, high-quality 3D first-person fighting game with brutal-feeling melee combat, satisfying combos, blood effects, intelligent enemies, smooth animations, and excellent mobile controls.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable browser and Android first-person fighting game, preferably as one self-contained HTML file.

## Requirements
- Three.js r128 via CDN without ES modules; responsive mobile controls, menus, settings, game modes, combat, AI, progression, effects, and audio.
- Test gameplay and fix bugs; save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px.

## Decisions
- Implemented the game in `index.html` using procedural Three.js geometry and Web Audio.
- Use `https://unpkg.com/three@0.128.0/build/three.min.js` after cdnjs returned 404.
- Reduced arena lighting and tone-mapping exposure after screenshots appeared overexposed.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented arena, first-person arms, player movement/look, attacks, blocks/parries, dodges, health/stamina, enemy types/AI, combos/finishers, hit effects, modes, progression, styles/shop, settings, pause/result screens, and mobile controls.
- JavaScript syntax checked; previous browser reload showed no runtime JavaScript errors.
- Captured menu, arena, start, combat, and latest validation JPEG screenshots under `/tmp/opencode/`.
- Browser test confirmed pause opens; no JavaScript page errors observed during latest test.

### Active
- Fix and retest pause/resume interaction; latest browser test found the hidden result overlay intercepts clicks on `#resume`.
- Continue gameplay validation against a nearby enemy and verify damage/defeat and round progression.
- Test mobile viewport/control layout; inspect latest screenshot/console and review `git status`.

### Blocked
- Pause/resume retest is blocked by `#result` overlay interception: Playwright reported `#again` from the hidden result subtree intercepting the `#resume` click.
- Enemy damage/defeat and mobile layout remain unverified.

## Next Move
1. Investigate overlay CSS and fix why hidden `#result` intercepts clicks; rerun pause/resume test.
2. Run gameplay test with enough time/close range to confirm damage, defeat, and round progression.
3. Validate mobile controls/layout, inspect screenshot and console, then check `git status`.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/game-check.mjs`: temporary Playwright gameplay, pause, and screenshot validation script.
- `/tmp/opencode/iron-veil-validation.jpeg`: latest gameplay validation screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/iron-veil-menu.jpeg`: menu screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/iron-veil-arena.jpeg`: arena screenshot.

## Objective
- Build and validate a complete, playable browser and Android first-person fighting game, preferably in one self-contained HTML file.

## Requirements
- Three.js r128 via CDN without ES modules; responsive mobile controls, menus, settings, game modes, combat, AI, progression, effects, and audio.
- Test gameplay and fix bugs; save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px.

## Decisions
- Implemented the game in `index.html` using procedural Three.js geometry and Web Audio.
- Use `https://unpkg.com/three@0.128.0/build/three.min.js` after cdnjs returned 404.
- Reduced arena lighting and tone-mapping exposure after screenshots appeared overexposed.
- Added `visibility:hidden` to hidden screen and overlay CSS states to prevent invisible dialogs from intercepting clicks.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented arena, first-person arms, player movement/look, attacks, blocks/parries, dodges, health/stamina, enemy types/AI, combos/finishers, hit effects, modes, progression, styles/shop, settings, pause/result screens, and mobile controls.
- JavaScript syntax checked; previous browser reload showed no runtime JavaScript errors.
- Captured menu, arena, start, combat, and validation JPEG screenshots under `/tmp/opencode/`.
- Pause/resume issue from the hidden result overlay was addressed with CSS visibility handling.

### Active
- Validate gameplay damage, enemy defeat, and round progression.
- Validate mobile controls and layout, including touch control overlap with the pause button.
- Review the latest test results and `git status`.

### Blocked
- Latest Playwright test could not click `#pauseBtn` at a 640×400 viewport because `#touchLook` intercepted pointer events; pause/resume and mobile checks did not complete.
- The latest gameplay test ran attacks but failed before printing its captured health/enemy state, so damage and defeat remain unverified.

## Next Move
1. Retest pause/resume at desktop viewport after the hidden-overlay CSS change.
2. Fix or verify the mobile `#touchLook` area does not intercept `#pauseBtn`, then test mobile controls/layout.
3. Run a focused combat test and confirm damage, defeat, and story round progression; inspect errors and screenshots.
4. Review `git status --short` and preserve existing untracked work.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/game-check.mjs`: Playwright gameplay, pause, and mobile validation script.
- `/tmp/opencode/iron-veil-validation.jpeg`: latest existing gameplay validation screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/iron-veil-menu.jpeg`: menu screenshot.

- `/tmp/opencode/iron-veil-start.jpeg`: started-game screenshot.

- A Playwright test using a higher-resolution viewport caused Chromium GPU process usage to spike; the later run used 640×400 and Low quality.
- The latest test reached attack iterations, then timed out with `#touchLook` intercepting the `#pauseBtn` click.

## Objective
- Build and validate a complete, playable browser and Android first-person fighting game, preferably in one self-contained HTML file.

## Requirements
- Three.js r128 via CDN without ES modules; responsive mobile controls, menus, settings, game modes, combat, AI, progression, effects, and audio.
- Test gameplay and fix bugs; save JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px.

## Decisions
- Implemented the game in `index.html` using procedural Three.js geometry and Web Audio.
- Use `https://unpkg.com/three@0.128.0/build/three.min.js` after cdnjs returned 404.
- Reduced arena lighting and tone-mapping exposure after screenshots appeared overexposed.
- Added hidden-state visibility handling to prevent invisible dialogs from intercepting clicks.
- Adjusted mobile `#touchLook` to start below the pause button, resolving their overlap.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the arena, first-person arms, player movement/look, attacks, blocks/parries, dodges, health/stamina, enemy types/AI, combos/finishers, hit effects, modes, progression, styles/shop, settings, pause/result screens, and mobile controls.
- JavaScript syntax checked; latest browser tests reported no page errors.

### Active
- Validate actual combat damage, enemy defeat, and story round progression.
- Verify pause/resume with a real pointer interaction; a Playwright click previously timed out with the canvas intercepting `#pauseBtn`.

### Blocked
- Combat damage and defeat are unverified: attacks reduced stamina but enemies remained at two, and player health stayed at 100.
- A focused retest may need positioning/aiming adjustments; the prior test did not confirm player movement toward the opponents.

## Next Move
1. Run a focused combat test that confirms player positioning/facing, enemy health loss, knockout, and story round progression.
2. Resolve the real-click pause test issue and verify resume.
3. Review `git status --short` and preserve existing untracked work.
